text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Cement company Cimpor owes six billion escudos in corporation tax (IRC) from 1990 and 1991.
- Banco de Fomento & Exterior prepares to open new branches in Angola and Mozambique. The first new branch may open in October in Luanda.
- Opposition Social Democrats to focus its political attack on government on what sees as worsening crime situation in the country.
- Banking group Jorge de Mello sets up three holdings to bid for stakes in tobacco company Tabaqueira at its coming privatization..
- Portuguese food prices rose 4.05 percent more than Spain's in first quarter of 1996.
